newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban said to take three province centres.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban said to take three province centres.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic movement took three more northern provincial capitals on Sunday in a weekend sweep that earlier conquered two major opposition strongholds, Taleban officials and a news service said.

The towns of Kunduz and Baghlan, capitals of provinces of the same name, came under Taleban control after fighters of opposition Hezb-i-Islami faction joined the purist Islamic militia, a senior Taleban official said.
A Pakistan-based private Afghan news service said the whole provinces of Kunduz and Baghlan and nearby Samangan province, including its capital Aibak, had also fallen to the Taleban on Sunday.

"Former Hezb-i-Islami fighters in Kunduz and Baghlan have joined the Taleban and the towns are now under their control," the Taleban official, Mullah Wakil Ahmed Motawakil, told Reuters by telephone from the militia headquarters in the southern city of Kandahar.

The advance of the Taleban has left the opposition in disarray, leaving less than 10 percent of Afghanistan under its control and many lines of communication to its remaining strongholds vulnerable to Taleban attacks.

The Hezb, led by Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, prime minister in a parallel opposition government, has been an uneasy ally of the other members of the opposition alliance, which includes Uzbek chief General Abdul Rashid Dostum's Jumbish-i-Milli movement and ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani's Jamiat-i-Islami.
Motawakil said people had risen also in the opposition-held Takhar province, on the edge of mountainous opposition-held eastern province of Badakhshan.
"In Takhar, people have also risen in our cause," he said. There was no independent confirmation of Motawakil's comments.
On Saturday, forces allied with the Taleban took Dostum's stronghold of Mazar-i-Sharif, capital of Balkh province, and Shibarghan, his military headquarters and capital of Jozjan province.
Mazar-i-Sharif was the last major town to hold out against the Taleban.

An official speaking from Mazar-i-Sharif said the town was now under the joint control of the Taleban and General Abdul Malik, Dostum's former foreign minister and deputy whose mutiny last week triggered the new Taleban advance.
Malik has been named deputy foreign minister in the Taleban government in Kabul.
"The area is under the joint command of the forces of General Malik and the Taleban," an aide to Malik said on Sunday morning.
"Dostum has fled to an unidentified location with his family and KGB comrades." said the aide, referring to Dostum's past association with the communists.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted its sources in Afghanistan as saying the entire province of Kunduz was captured by the Taleban after light clashes. But the militia had to overcome stiff resistance to capture Samangan province.
